extDescription.message: Puts a red box around fake look-alike links (paypa1.com, pаypal.com...) and blocks them until you really confirm.

badgeDanger.message: Grilled Phish: FAKE or dangerous website

rIp.message: The link goes to a bare number address instead of a website name. Real companies do not do this.

rScript.message: The address mixes letters from different alphabets ($1). This is a classic trick to fake a famous name.

rHomoglyph.message: It uses look-alike letters from another alphabet to imitate "$1".

rSameLabel.message: It uses the name "$1" but it is NOT $2's real website.

rSwap.message: It swaps letters to look like "$1" (tricks like "rn" for "m", "1" for "l", "0" for "o").

rTypo.message: The name "$1" is one letter different from "$2".

rBrandSub.message: "$1" appears at the start of the address, but the site really belongs to "$2".

rBait.message: It adds words to the name "$1" to look official, but it is not $2's website.

rTextMismatch.message: The text says "$1", but the link secretly goes to "$2".

rAge.message: This website was created $1. Scam websites are usually brand new and vanish within days; real banks and shops have existed for years.

rDbSub.message: It starts with "$1", a well-known website, but the site really belongs to "$2".

rDbLook.message: It looks almost identical to "$1", a well-known website, but some letters are different.

optIntro.message: Add the websites you really use: your bank, your email, your shop. Grilled Phish will then block any fake copy of them, even with one changed letter.

optHint.message: Big companies (PayPal, Google, Amazon, Poste Italiane, banks…) are already protected.

optLearn.message: 📖 How to spot a scam website: a 5-minute guide

optBadAddr.message: That does not look like a website address. Try something like "mybank.com".

optAgeP.message: Most scam websites are created a few days before the attack and disappear soon after. Grilled Phish can check when a website was created and block very new ones.

optAgeCheck.message: Block websites that are newer than

optAgePrivacy.message: Privacy: to do this, only the website's name (for example best-deals.shop, never the full address or what you do there) is sent to the official registry for that ending, such as Verisign for .com. Some endings (.it, .de, .es, .eu) don't publish creation dates, so those sites can't be checked.

optDbP.message: Grilled Phish knows the most visited websites in the world, so it can block copies of them (for example wikipedla.org pretending to be wikipedia.org). The check happens on your computer.

optAuto.message: Keep this list up to date automatically (recommended)

optSigned.message: Updates are digitally signed by Grilled Phish. A list that isn't correctly signed, is older than the one you have, or looks damaged is refused, and the current list stays in use.

aboutH.message: 🛡️ Grilled Phish will never contact you

aboutData.message: We never collect your data. There is no account and no Grilled Phish server: nothing about you or the websites you visit ever reaches us.

aboutWrite.message: We never write to you or call you. No emails, text messages, chats or phone calls. We never ask for passwords, codes, money or access to your computer.

aboutLinks.message: We never send you links. Grilled Phish only shows links inside the extension itself.

aboutOff.message: Nobody from Grilled Phish will ever ask you to turn it off, remove it or mark a website as trusted.

aboutScam.message: If someone contacts you saying they are from Grilled Phish, it is a scam.
